questions.q: If $$9^{x^{2}+2x-3}-4(3^{x^{2}+2x-2})+27=0$$ then the product of all possible values of x is
questions.solution: Put t = 3^(x²+2x−3). The equation becomes t²−12t+27=0, so t=3 or 9. Hence x solves x²+2x−4=0 or x²+2x−5=0. The root products are −4 and −5; their combined product is 20.

questions.q: The average number of copies of a book sold per day by a shopkeeper is 60 in the initial seven days and 63 in the initial eight days, after the book launch. On the ninth day, she sells 11 copies less than the eighth day, and the average number of copies sold per day from second day to ninth day becomes 66. The number of copies sold on the first day of the book launch is
questions.solution: The first seven days total 7×60=420 books; the first eight total 8×63=504. Day eight sold 84 and day nine sold 73. All nine days total 577. Days two to nine total 8×66=528, leaving 49 for day one.

questions.q: The set of all real values of x for which $$(x^{2}-| x+9|+x)>0$$, is
questions.solution: For x≥−9, the inequality becomes x²−9>0, giving x<−3 or x>3 within that range. For x<−9, it becomes x²+2x+9>0, which is always true. Combine the ranges: x<−3 or x>3.

questions.q: An item with a cost price of Rs. 1650 is sold at a certain discount on a fixed marked price to earn a profit of 20% on the cost price. If the discount was doubled, the profit would have been Rs. 110. The rate of discount, in percentage, at which the profit percentage would be equal to the rate of discount, is nearest to
questions.solution: The first selling price is 1650×1.20 = ₹1980. Doubling the discount reduces it to ₹1760, so the original discount amount is ₹220 and marked price is ₹2200. If the required rate is r%, set 2200(1−r/100)=1650(1+r/100). This gives r=100/7≈14.29%, nearest to 14.

questions.q: If m and n are integers such that $$(m+2n)(2m+n)=27$$, then the maximum possible value of $$2m-3n$$ is
questions.solution: Let A=m+2n and B=2m+n, so AB=27, m=(2B−A)/3 and n=(2A−B)/3. Enumerate the positive and negative factor pairs of 27 that give integer m,n. The maximum occurs at m=1,n=−5, giving 2m−3n=17.

questions.q: The sum of digits of the number $$(625)^{65} \times (128)^{36}$$ is
questions.solution: 625=5⁴ and 128=2⁷, so the product is 5²⁶⁰×2²⁵²=5⁸×10²⁵². The nonzero digit block is 390625; its digits sum to 25.

questions.q: The equations $$3x^{2}-5x+p=0$$ and $$2x^{2}-2x+q=0$$ have one common root. The sum of the other roots of this equations is
questions.solution: Let the common root be r. Subtract 3/2 times the second equation from the first to get −2r+p−3q/2=0. The total of both pairs of roots is 5/3+1=8/3. Remove the common root twice: the sum sought is 8/3−p+3q/2.

questions.q: If $\log_{64}(x^2)+\log_8(\sqrt{y})+3\log_{512}(\sqrt{y}z)=4$, where x, y and z are positive real numbers, then the minimum possible value of $(x+y+z)$ is
questions.solution: Convert all logarithms to base 2. Their sum is (log₂x+log₂y+log₂z)/3=4, so xyz=4096. AM–GM gives x+y+z≥3×16=48, achieved at x=y=z=16.

questions.q: Rita and Sneha can row a boat at 5 km/h and 6 km/h in still water, respectively. In a river flowing with a constant velocity, Sneha takes 48 minutes more to row 14 km upstream than to row the same distance downstream. If Rita starts from a certain location in the river, and returns downstream to the same location, taking a total of 100 minutes, then the total distance, in km, Rita will cover is
questions.solution: Let stream speed be v. Sneha’s time difference gives 14/(6−v)−14/(6+v)=4/5 hour, with positive solution v=1 km/h. Rita travels upstream at 4 and downstream at 6 km/h. If one-way distance is d, d/4+d/6=5/3, so d=4. Total distance is 8 km.

questions.q: Suppose a,b,c are three distinct natural numbers, such that $$3ac=8(a+b)$$. Then, the smallest possible value of $$3a+2b+c$$ is
questions.solution: Rearrange to b=a(3c−8)/8. For c≤2, b cannot be positive. For a=1 the smallest valid c is 8, giving objective 15. For a=2,c=4, b=1 and the objective is 12. Any a≥3 with positive, distinct b,c has objective at least 14. The minimum is 12.

questions.q: Let $$f(x)=\frac{x}{(2x-1)}$$ and $$g(x)=\frac{x}{(x-1)}$$. Then the domain of the function $$h(x)=f(g(x))+g(f(x))$$ is all real numbers except
questions.solution: The inner functions require x≠1 and x≠1/2. For f(g(x)), its outer denominator also vanishes at x=−1. For g(f(x)), the outer denominator vanishes at x=1. Thus exclude −1,1/2,1.

questions.q: A loan of Rs 1000 is fully repaid by two installments of Rs 530 and Rs 594, paid at the end of first and second year, respectively. If the interest is compounded annually, then the rate of interest, in percentage, is
questions.solution: Let the annual growth factor be t. Present values give 530/t+594/t²=1000. The positive root of 1000t²−530t−594=0 is t=1.08. The interest rate is 8%.

questions.q: Two tangents drawn from a point P and a circle with center O at point Q and R. Point A and B lie on PQ and PR, repectively, such that AB is also a tangent to the same circle. If $$\angle AOB=50^{0}$$, then $$\angle APB$$, in degrees equals
questions.solution: The centre lies on the external angle bisectors at A and B of triangle PAB, giving ∠AOB=90°−∠APB/2. Therefore 50=90−∠APB/2 and ∠APB=80°.

questions.q: The number of divisors of $$(2^{6}\times 3^{5}\times 5^{3}\times 7^{2})$$, which are of the form $$(3r+1)$$, where r is a non-negative integer, is
questions.solution: A divisor congruent to 1 modulo 3 cannot contain any factor 3. Factors 2 and 5 both equal −1 modulo 3, so their exponents must have an even sum. There are 14 such exponent pairs and 3 choices for the exponent of 7. Count = 14×3 = 42.

questions.q: Let ABCDEF be a regular hexagon and P and Q be the midpoints of AB and CD, respectively. Then, the ratio of the areas of trapezium PBCQ and hexagon ABCDEF is
questions.solution: Take side length 1. With coordinates A=(1,0), B=(1/2,√3/2), C=(−1/2,√3/2), D=(−1,0), the midpoints are P=(3/4,√3/4), Q=(−3/4,√3/4). Trapezium area is 5√3/16 and hexagon area is 3√3/2. Their ratio is 5:24.

questions.q: If a,b,c and d are integers such that their sum is 46, then the minimum possible value of $$(a-b)^{2}+(a-c)^{2}+(a-d)^{2}$$ is
questions.solution: A value 0 would require all four integers equal, impossible with sum 46. A value 1 would make exactly one of b,c,d differ from a by 1, forcing an odd sum. The choice a=12,b=11,c=11,d=12 gives 1+1+0=2, the minimum.

questions.q: The ratio of expenditures of Lakshmi and Meenakshi is 2 : 3, and the ratio of income of Lakshmi to expenditure of Meenakshi is 6 : 7. If excess of income over expenditure is saved by Lakshmi and Meenakshi, and the ratio of their savings is 4 : 9, then the ratio of their incomes is
questions.solution: Let expenditures be 14 and 21. Lakshmi’s income is 18, so her savings are 4. Meenakshi saves 9 and earns 21+9=30. Their income ratio is 18:30=3:5.

questions.q: Let $$a_{n}$$ be the $$n^{th}$$ term of a decreasing infinite geometric progression. If $$a_{1}+a_{2}+a_{3}=52$$ and $$a_{1}a_{2}+a_{2}a_{3}+a_{3}a_{1}=624$$, then the sum of this geometric progression is
questions.solution: Write the first three terms as a,ar,ar². Their pairwise-product sum is ar(a+ar+ar²)=52ar=624, so ar=12. Then a+12+144/a=52 gives a=36 or 4. The decreasing progression uses a=36, r=1/3. Infinite sum = 36/(1−1/3)=54.

questions.q: A mixture of coffee and cocoa, 16% of which is coffee, costs Rs 240 per kg. Another mixture of coffee and cocoa, of which 36% is coffee, costs Rs 320 per kg. If a new mixture of coffee and cocoa costs Rs 376 per kg, then the quantity, in kg, of coffee in 10 kg of this new mixture is
questions.solution: A 20 percentage-point increase in coffee raises the price by ₹80/kg, so pure coffee costs ₹400/kg more than cocoa. Cocoa price is 240−0.16×400=₹176/kg. At ₹376/kg, coffee share is (376−176)/400=1/2. Ten kg therefore contains 5 kg of coffee.

questions.q: In $$\triangle ABC$$, points D and E are on the sides BC and AC, respectively. BE and AD intersect at point T such that AD:AT=4:3, and BE:BT=5:4. Point F lies on AC such that DF is parallel to BE. Then, BD:CD is
questions.solution: Use triangle mass points. AT:TD=3:1 gives mass(D)=3 mass(A). BT:TE=4:1 gives mass(E)=4 mass(B). Since mass(E)=mass(A)+mass(C) and mass(D)=mass(B)+mass(C), setting mass(A)=5 gives mass(B)=4 and mass(C)=11. Thus BD:CD=mass(C):mass(B)=11:4.

questions.q: Ankita is twice as efficient as Bipin, while Bipin is twice as efficient as Chandan. All three of them start together on a job, and Bipin leaves the job after 20 days. If the job got completed in 60 days, the number of days needed by Chandan to complete the job alone, is
questions.solution: Use daily work rates Chandan=1, Bipin=2, Ankita=4 units. All three work for 20 days and the other two for 40 days. Total work = 7×20+5×40=340 units. Chandan alone needs 340 days.

questions.q: A certain amount of money was divided among Pinu, Meena, Rinu and Seema. Pinu received 20% of the total amount and Meena received 40% of the remaining amount. If Seema received 20% less than Pinu, the ratio of the amounts received by Pinu and Rinu is
questions.solution: Use total 100. Pinu receives 20 and Meena receives 40% of 80=32. Seema receives 16, leaving 32 for Rinu. Pinu:Rinu=20:32=5:8.
